title: Highest Peaks by Continent
intro: Ten questions on the highest mountains of the continents and where they stand. Heights are as recorded by Natural Earth. Every answer shows its source.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest mountain in the world?
questions.explain: Mount Everest is 8,848 m on the Natural Earth data; K2 follows at 8,611 m.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest peak of South America?
Which is the highest peak of North America?
questions.explain: Denali in Alaska is 6,194 m; Mount Logan in Canada is 5,959 m.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest peak of Africa?
questions.explain: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is 5,895 m; Mount Kenya is 5,199 m.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest peak of Europe in this data?
questions.explain: Elbrus in Russia is 5,642 m, higher than Mont Blanc in the Alps (4,806 m).

questions.prompt: Which is the highest peak of Antarctica?
questions.explain: Vinson Massif is 4,892 m, the highest point of the continent.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest peak of Oceania in this data?
questions.explain: Puncak Jaya in Indonesia is 4,884 m; Mount Wilhelm is 4,509 m and Aoraki / Mount Cook 3,754 m.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is the second highest in the Natural Earth data?
questions.explain: K2 on the China-Pakistan border is 8,611 m, just ahead of Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).

questions.prompt: Which of these 8,000 m peaks lies entirely within Nepal?
questions.explain: Dhaulagiri is wholly in Nepal; Everest is on the Nepal-China border, Kanchenjunga on the Nepal-India border and K2 on the China-Pakistan border.

questions.prompt: Which of these Andean giants stands on the border of Argentina and Chile?
questions.explain: Ojos del Salado is 6,880 m; Aconcagua lies wholly in Argentina, Huascaran in Peru and Nevado Sajama in Bolivia.
